title: Vortex screening and the fate of the BKT transition with long-range couplings
abstract: The stability of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless phase against long-range interactions remains an open problem. We address this question in the two-dimensional XY model with couplings decaying as $r^{-2-σ}$, by developing a real-space renormalization-group treatment near the Gaussian manifold of quasi-long-range ordered (QLRO) states. We retain the full many-body vortex interaction and show that, at leading order in the fugacity, screening by small vortex--antivortex pairs preserves its Gaussian-average representation without an expansion in the long-range coupling. Including spin waves perturbatively then yields a local stability criterion: a stable QLRO interval exists only for $σ>7/4$. We also investigate a Wilson--Fisher-like fixed point at finite coupling for $σ<7/4$, for which the retained flow predicts $ν^{-1}\sim\sqrt{7/4-σ}$ as it merges with the Gaussian line.
summary: This work addresses the stability of the BKT phase in 2D XY models with long-range couplings using a real-space renormalization group approach. By analyzing vortex screening, the authors derive a critical condition ($\sigma > 7/4$) for the persistence of QLRO. The findings establish a detailed phase diagram, predicting a crossover to a Wilson-Fisher-like fixed point when the coupling decay is too slow.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase, characterized by Quasi-Long-Range Order (QLRO), when the system is subjected to long-range interactions decaying as $r^{-2-\sigma}$.
main_result: A stable Gaussian QLRO phase is found to exist only for coupling decay exponents $\sigma > 7/4$; otherwise, the system flows towards a finite-coupling, Wilson-Fisher-like fixed point.
method: The analysis employs a real-space renormalization-group (RG) treatment, incorporating the full many-body vortex interaction and perturbatively including spin-wave contributions.
model_or_system: The model is the two-dimensional XY model with a ferromagnetic Hamiltonian featuring long-range couplings $J(r) \sim r^{-2-\sigma}$. The physics is analyzed by decomposing the field into smooth spin-wave and discrete vortex components.
key_observables: The primary observables are the renormalization of the spin stiffness ($J$) and the vortex fugacity ($y$), which determine the stability of the QLRO phase.
important_parameters: The critical exponent $\sigma$ governing the decay of the long-range coupling, and the RG flow parameters $J_\ell, y_\ell, g_\ell$.
main_assumptions: The analysis retains the full many-body vortex interaction and assumes that the vortex screening process preserves the Gaussian-average representation of the partition function.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the renormalization procedure, showing how integrating out vortex-antivortex pairs screens the interaction and renormalizes the spin stiffness $J_\ell$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by defining the model and the RG framework. It details the vortex screening mechanism, deriving the stability criterion ($\sigma > 7/4$). Finally, it analyzes the RG flow, predicting the existence and nature of a finite-coupling fixed point for $\sigma < 7/4$.
why_interesting: The rigorous RG treatment of vortex screening in the presence of long-range interactions provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding phase transitions in 2D systems, connecting concepts from Coulomb gases to critical phenomena.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of the renormalization procedure. Spin configurations before (left) and after (right) integrating out a vortex–antivortex pair, with positive and negative vortices marked in red and blue. The yellow surface symbolically represents the many-body vortex interaction. Integrating out the pair screens this interaction by decreasing the spin stiffness Jℓ.

FIG. 2. RG flows and phase structure. (a) Trajectories at σ = 1.85, colored according to their LR (teal), QLRO (ochre), or disordered (gray) basin. (b) Fixed-point locus as σ varies (pink): the LR-marginal endpoint of the Gaussian line, J = [2π(2 −σ)]−1, g = y = 0, for 7/4 < σ < 2, joins the finite-coupling branch for σ < 7/4 at JBKT = 2/π. The nearby saddle flow is schematic. (c) Illustrative numerical RG phase diagram for J0 = 1/T, g0 = 10−4/T, and y0 = e−6/T , with the same color code.
